title: What does the XRPL DisallowIncomingPayChan account flag mean?
abstract: Sourced explanation of DisallowIncomingPayChan and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, DisallowIncomingPayChan blocks new incoming payment channels under the DisallowIncoming feature. [1]

A payment channel locks XRP for cumulative claims, which is different from a direct XRP Payment. Blocking channel creation does not mean all XRP receipts are prohibited. Existing channels have their own claim and closure rules. Confirm the actual ledger setting and intended transaction type before assuming a counterparty can open a channel to this recipient. [1][2]

XRPL distinguishes an AccountSet option from the AccountRoot bit that records the resulting state. SetFlag and ClearFlag use option identifiers, while the ledger Flags field stores bit values; the numbers are not interchangeable. Read the documented mapping for DisallowIncomingPayChan and check the validated account state after any permitted change. A successful submission response alone does not establish that the requested state is final. [1][2]

Author interpretation: document why DisallowIncomingPayChan is needed, who may authorize a change and what existing users would experience. Review irreversible settings before issuance and test reversible settings with representative counterparties. This is guidance for interpreting account controls, not a live network measurement. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
